output.brief: The overrun mostly comes from ending the after-hours closing contract, not from the hiring freeze. From 1 April, closing at 41 sites moved to maintenance staff as call-backs with a 3-hour minimum. Call-back pay rose from $38k to $289k. 1,962 call-backs carry the closing code, and none are in Summit Hill, which kept its contract. Regular holdover hours rose only 1.5%, so vacancies and the hot summer don't explain the jump. Eastgate has just 1 vacancy yet shows one of the largest call-back increases. Internal Audit checked the fraud allegation against lock logs and found no padding, so don't discipline the two named employees. Restore contracted closing (extension or re-tender) and track call-back spend. The contract saved $96k but call-backs cost roughly $250k more. Don't impose an overtime cap: crews would stop taking closings, which the liability coverage requires. The favoritism claim in Eastgate is unproven, because sign-up sheets were discarded. Keep and review the sheets, and make the sign-up fair, before any action against the supervisor. The injury link to overtime is plausible but unproven. Match claims to individual hours. Granting the eleven-position exemption wouldn't fix the main driver.
